title: Make interrupted jobs retryable and picked up by drain
summary: A job left in dispatched state with no live process (interrupted, e.g. by a container restart) can be retried with `athena retry <job>` without first being closed by hand, and `athena drain` picks such jobs back up and works them. The audience is the user running athena on a machine that can restart.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for retry of interrupted and drain pickup; cargo test and clippy criterion.
Criteria run retry and drain against an interrupted job rather than checking wiring.
Fixes the retry gate and the drain queue, not just the one job.
One focused change on retry eligibility and drain pickup.
Behavior criteria name cargo test commands.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Resume is done as a retry: a new job 'try again on <id>' is read, carrying the interrupted job's request; the interrupted job is then closed with an explanatory outcome (superseded by the retry) so it stops showing as open.
'Interrupted' means state Dispatched with no entry in the process registry, as status.rs already defines it; a job whose process is live is still refused.
Drain picks up interrupted jobs on the drained channels (steward and user queue) in the same ordering as queued work, using its existing retry path.
An interrupted job has no verification or outcome record, so earlier_attempt must accept that case and carry only the request and any corrections.
The closing of the interrupted job by retry/drain reuses the existing close mechanism and records.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test (run with cargo test) creates a job that is dispatched with no live process, runs `athena retry <job>`, and gets a proposal whose request is 'try again on <id>' carrying the original request, instead of the error 'only a rejected or failed job can be tried again'.
A test (cargo test) shows that a job whose process is still in the registry (running) is still refused by retry with a clear message.

A drain test (cargo test) with an interrupted job on a drained channel shows the drain lists it as work, retries it, and does not report an empty queue; an interrupted job on another channel is left alone.
The `athena status` next-step hint for 'interrupted' (status.rs) and the run.rs interrupted message mention retry as the way to resume, alongside close.
drain.rs module docs and CHANGELOG.md describe interrupted jobs being retryable and drained.
cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check all pass.

out_of_scope: Fixing the plan/drain read-request bug from job 20261016-071045-mx7e
Automatically resuming a job mid-run from its partial invocation state
Changing retry for already rejected or failed jobs
departures: Touches retry, status and drain across crates with an ambiguous resume-vs-retry design, so cost and time are above the reference and pass odds lower.
